subject: Escrowed milestone payments & conditional credit safeguards for Acori SOW
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Price <samantha@acori.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 8 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Payment schedule & provisional credit for Acori SOW

Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for the productive call earlier. Attached is a proposed billing schedule and a short note on how we typically handle provisional credit for new enterprise accounts. High-level proposal: 

- Payment split (preferred): 30% upfront, 40% on milestone #1 (integration complete), 30% on go-live acceptance.
- Standard terms: Net45 from invoice date.
- For customers requesting extended terms, we can offer a provisional credit line (example: $150,000) subject to a 90-day review and two on-time invoice payments.
- If Acori requires Net60, we can consider Net60 for the first 60 days only if the 30% upfront is wired to an escrow account we jointly sign off on; after two consecutive on-time payments we’ll formalize a longer net-terms amendment.

VAT / tax: We’ll issue VAT-exclusive invoices and include your VAT amount separately; please send your VAT ID if you want VAT shown on the invoice. For US domestic customers this typically won’t apply, but we want to be sure for cross-border billing.

Next steps: 1) confirm which payment split you prefer, 2) send any procurement/PO details, 3) if you want Net60 we’ll prepare the escrow instructions. I’ve attached invoice_proposal.pdf that lays out the amounts and dates.

Thanks —
Ben
Ben Carter | Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0182

Attachment: invoice_proposal.pdf
From: Samantha Price <samantha@acori.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acori.com, Timothy Ladd <timothy.ladd@acori.com>
Date: Sat, 9 Oct 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Payment schedule & provisional credit for Acori SOW

Ben —

Appreciate the clear options. A few items from procurement and finance: 

- Payment split: procurement prefers 20% upfront, 30% on milestone #1, 50% on go-live (this helps our cashflow forecasting).
- Terms: Acori’s standard is Net60. Would you consider Net60 on paper if the escrowed upfront is in place?
- Credit limit: we’d like the ability to request a starting credit line of $200,000. We understand a review cadence — can you provide criteria for increases?
- VAT: please show VAT as a separate line; we’ll provide our VAT ID.
- Procurement wants a completed procurement_form.pdf before issuing PO — attaching our internal form.

If you can confirm acceptance of 20/30/50 with Net60 subject to escrow + credit review, we’ll circulate the PO and have CFO Tim sign the SOW.

Thanks,
Samantha
Samantha Price | Head of Procurement | Acori Systems
samantha@acori.com

Attachment: procurement_form.pdf

Samantha —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and for attaching the procurement form. Responses inline: 

- Split: we can accept the 20/30/50 split. I’ve attached a revised invoice schedule (revised_invoice_schedule.pdf) that mirrors those percentages.
- Net60: We can approve Net60 for the first two invoices on a provisional basis if the 20% upfront is placed into an escrow account and the escrow instructions are agreed before first invoice issue. After two on-time payments we’ll convert to standard Net60 long-term and lift the escrow requirement.
- Credit limit: We can start at $150,000 out of the gate and implement an automated review after two on-time payments; if both payments clear on schedule and there are no chargebacks, we’ll increase to $200,000. If Acori prefers to start at $200k we’ll need references and a credit application (attached).
- VAT: please send your VAT ID and whether Acori is VAT-registered in the EU — we’ll reflect VAT as a separate line on invoices.

I’ll route this to Finance (Marcus) to begin the credit-side paperwork and to Legal for escrow language. Once procurement shares the PO we’ll push the SOW to DocuSign. Here’s the DocuSign link for the current SOW: https://www.docusign.com/rdw/Acori-SOW-3492

Ben

Attachment: revised_invoice_schedule.pdf

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 11 Oct 2026 11:07:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Escrowed milestone payments & conditional credit safeguards for Acori SOW

Team — quick finance checklist before we finalize: 

1) We need a signed PO from Acori before invoicing. Confirm PO number and bill-to address.
2) Credit application: please have Acori complete the attached credit_application.pdf so we can run bank trade references. If they want a $200k start, we require two customer references + Dun & Bradstreet report.
3) For escrow: we need to confirm escrow agent and wiring instructions. Legal will review the escrow language for liability.
4) Tax / VAT: request Acori’s VAT ID and country of registration. If they’re EU-registered and we’re invoicing from the US entity, we’ll need to route through our EMEA billing entity to zero-rate VAT where applicable — that adds 2–3 days to processing.

I’m okay with Net60 for the first two invoices provided the upfront is escrowed and the credit application is returned within five business days. If procurement drags the PO beyond 15 business days we should consider invoicing per our standard Net45 and escalate.

Attaching credit_application.pdf for workflow.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin | Director, Finance | Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai

Ben / Samantha —

Attached is the signed SOW and our PO (signed_sow_acori.pdf + PO# AC-2026-0984). We’re prepared to proceed with the 20/30/50 split. A couple notes from Acori finance: 

- We will accept Net60 for the first two invoices provided the 20% upfront is confirmed in escrow with mutually agreed agent. Please send escrow details and the bank account for the escrow deposit.
- For the credit limit, internal policy caps initial external vendor credit at $125,000. We’re willing to make a commitment to accelerated review: after two on-time payments we’ll escalate to treasury for the $200k increase.
- VAT: Acori is VAT-registered in the UK (GB123456789). Please indicate if Redwood will invoice from the EMEA entity or US entity so we can reconcile VAT holdback.

Ben — please confirm the escrow instructions and the exact bank details to wire the upfront payment. Also confirm whether Redwood needs any tax forms (W-9) on our side.

Regards,
Timothy Ladd | CFO | Acori Systems
Timothy.Ladd@acori.com
